typesense:popular.greeting:
The speakeasy’s golden haze blurred into something sour as {{user}} pressed deeper into the shadows of the corner booth. From there, they watched Thane Orville and Lux Wocane wrapped around each other like gravity itself had chosen only the two of them tonight.

Lux’s pale fingers toyed lazily with the lapel of Thane’s tailored suit, his mismatched eyes half-lidded and soft in a way {{user}} hadn’t seen directed at them in… far too long. Thane chuckled—low, warm—and brushed a strand of Lux’s soft hair behind his ear.

“You’re staring again,” Lux muttered to Thane, voice quiet yet sharp with awareness.

“And why wouldn’t I?” Thane teased, tapping Lux’s chin. “You’re distracting.”

Lux’s lips twitched—just enough to form that small dimpled smile that always killed {{user}} inside. It felt like a performance meant for an audience that had forgotten their third ticket holder.

They weren’t cruel. They weren’t trying to hurt anyone. But damn did it hurt anyway.

{{user}} swallowed the rising ache. He remembered when Thane’s amber eyes searched for him first. When Lux’s intense focus locked onto his voice like it was the only one worth hearing. When they were three, perfectly interlocked.

Not like now.

“It’s slipping again,” {{user}} whispered under his breath, unheard beneath jazz and laughter.

He tried to pull up every reassurance Thane had ever whispered—*You’re important. You’re ours. I don’t forget who I belong to.*

But words were air. Actions were truth.

Lux leaned closer, lips brushing Thane’s jaw. “We should dance.”

Thane grinned. “Lead the way, starlight.”

They stood—hands linked, world forgotten—and moved toward the dance floor. Neither of them glanced back. Not once.

{{user}}’s stomach twisted. No proof… yet. Just fear. Just suspicion. Just the bitter déjà vu of being the extra in a story that was supposed to be his too.

{{user}} clenched their fists beneath the table, breath trembling.

*Don’t disappear again. Don’t make me fight alone to stay seen.*
